abstract: Background The efficacy and safety of ultrashort (≤1-month) dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) followed by antiplatelet monotherapy remain uncertain in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients. Objectives This study sought to compare ultrashort vs standard-duration DAPT in patients with ACS undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials until February 15, 2026. Primary outcomes were major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), major bleeding, and net adverse clinical event (NACE). Prespecified subgroup analyses examined by ethnicity (East Asian vs non-East Asian) and abbreviation strategy (intensive: ≤1-week DAPT or clopidogrel/aspirin monotherapy vs moderate: ≥2-week DAPT, followed by ticagrelor/prasugrel monotherapy). Results Across 10 trials (n = 29,232), ultrashort DAPT did not increase MACCE risk (HR: 1.06; 95% CI: 0.93-1.20; P = 0.38; I 2 = 24%), with higher MACCE risk observed in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) but not non-ST-segment elevation ACS (NSTE-ACS), and significantly reduced major bleeding (HR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.35-0.64; P 2 = 44%), resulting in a net clinical benefit (HR: 0.83; 95% CI: 0.72-0.97; P = 0.02; I 2 = 61%). Bleeding reduction was more pronounced in East Asians (HR: 0.35; 95% CI: 0.25-0.49; P 2 = 0%) than non-East Asians (HR: 0.63; 95% CI: 0.43-0.93; P = 0.02; I 2 = 44%), with a significant interaction (P = 0.02). The abbreviation strategy significantly modified outcomes (P for interaction = 0.003): intensive abbreviation raised MACCE risk (HR: 1.37; 95% CI: 1.11-1.69; P = 0.003; I 2 = 0%), while moderate abbreviation had no statistically significant difference (HR: 0.96; 95% CI: 0.85-1.08; P = 0.47; I 2 = 0%). Conclusions In patients with ACS undergoing PCI, ultrashort DAPT reduced bleeding without increasing ischemic events overall, although a signal of increased MACCE was observed in STEMI but not in NSTE-ACS. Bleeding reduction was greater in East Asians, while ≤1-week DAPT or clopidogrel/aspirin monotherapy may increase ischemic risk.

Clinical Performance and Reproducibility of the LIRA Method for TAVR in Bicuspid Anatomy
abstract: Background Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) anatomy remains challenging, with heterogeneous outcomes and no standardized sizing strategy. The LIRA (level of implantation at the raphe) method is a bicuspid-dedicated approach that complements standard annular sizing with a single perimeter measurement at the raphe level. A previous single-center experience suggested favorable results. Objectives The aim of this study was to evaluate clinical performance and reproducibility of the LIRA method for TAVR sizing in a large BAV multicenter cohort. Methods A total of 215 BAV patients undergoing TAVR with the LIRA method at 6 centers were retrospectively analyzed. Procedural and clinical outcomes were adjudicated according to Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria and assessed at 30 days and 1 year. Available full-cycle computed tomographic data sets from external centers were reanalyzed in a blinded centralized core laboratory to assess reproducibility of the LIRA method. Results The application of the LIRA method led to prosthesis downsizing in 74.4% of cases. At 30 days, device success was 93%, and moderate or greater paravalvular leak had occurred in 4.6% of patients, new permanent pacemaker implantation in 10.7%, and stroke in 1.9%. At 1 year, all-cause mortality was 5.7%, and clinical efficacy was observed in 92.8% of patients. Clinical outcomes were consistent across centers. Prosthesis sizing agreement was excellent (κ = 0.85; 95% CI: 0.74-0.96), and perimeter concordance was good (intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.76; 95% CI: 0.63-0.85). Conclusions In this large multicenter cohort, the LIRA method demonstrated good reproducibility across centers and was associated with favorable procedural and clinical outcomes in BAV patients undergoing TAVR. These findings support its clinical applicability as a bicuspid-dedicated sizing strategy.

title: Stenting Technique and Clinical Outcome in True Bifurcation PCI
abstract: Background Optimal stenting for true coronary bifurcation lesions is widely debated, with few studies using predefined intracoronary imaging. Objectives The aim of this study was to assess predictors and outcomes associated with a 1 vs a 2-stent technique and whether optical coherence tomographic (OCT) guidance modified the association with clinical outcomes. Methods This OCTOBER (European Trial on Optical Coherence Tomography Optimized Bifurcation Event Reduction; NCT03171311) post hoc analysis included 1,201 patients with true coronary bifurcation treated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Clinical outcomes were analyzed using multivariable Cox regression. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of a 2-stent technique. Results Clinical indication, left main coronary artery (LMCA) bifurcation, and side branch (SB) lesion severity were the strongest predictors of 2-stent use (acute clinical presentation: adjusted OR: 1.73 [95% CI: 1.33-2.25]; LMCA: adjusted OR: 2.04 [95% CI: 1.38-3.03]; SB lesion length: adjusted OR: 1.06 per mm [95% CI: 1.03-1.09]; SB diameter stenosis: adjusted OR: 1.04 per 1% [95% CI: 1.03-1.05]). In as-treated analysis, a 1-stent technique was associated with a lower 2-year rate of major adverse cardiac events (MACE) than a 2-stent technique (9.0% vs 13.9%; adjusted HR: 1.53; 95% CI: 1.04-2.27), with no interaction with OCT (P for interaction = 0.24). Planned-strategy analyses showed no significant difference in MACE. Among patients treated with a double kissing (DK)-crush technique, angiography-guided DK crush was associated with higher MACE rates compared with OCT-guided DK-crush (HR: 2.42; 95% CI: 1.12-5.24). Conclusions Clinical indication, LMCA bifurcation, and SB disease severity predicted 2-stent PCI. MACE did not differ according to planned strategy, whereas actual 2-stent PCI had higher MACE rates, likely reflecting a higher burden of complexity. The lowest event rates were observed with OCT-guided 1-stent PCI.

title: Residual Mitral Regurgitation as a Long-Term Predictor of Mortality After Mitral TEER
abstract: Background The MITRA-PRO registry revealed residual mitral regurgitation (MR) as an important predictor of 1-year and 3-year mortality following mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER). Objectives The 5-year follow-up of the MITRA-PRO registry (N = 1,491) aimed to assess the impact of residual MR on 5-year mortality. Furthermore, time-dependent predictors of mortality after M-TEER should be assessed. Methods Patients with a MitraScore of ≤3 were classified as patients with mild residual MR after M-TEER, while a MitraScore of ≥4 was defined as relevant residual MR. Adjusted HRs were calculated for multivariate analysis of time-dependent predictors. Results Five-year mortality was significantly lower in patients with mild or less residual MR compared with patients with more than mild residual MR (MitraScore ≤3 group: 55.1% vs MitraScore ≥4 group: 67.7%). The relationship between intraprocedural MitraScore after M-TEER and mortality was almost linear. In patients with degenerative MR, 5-year mortality was 53.1% in the MitraScore ≤3 group and 73.2% in the MitraScore ≥4 group. Regarding functional MR, the corresponding 5-year mortality rates were 55.0% and 64.6%. Mortality predictors after M-TEER were time dependent: Early risk was driven by advanced disease and procedural factors, whereas residual MR became prognostic after 30 days and remained associated with excess long-term mortality. Conclusions Residual MR assessed by intraprocedural MitraScore after M-TEER independently predicts 5-year mortality. This finding underscores the importance of achieving optimal MR reduction during M-TEER and supports quantitative multimodal intraprocedural assessment to guide strategy and improve long-term outcomes.

abstract: BACKGROUND: Up to 50% of pulmonary embolism (PE) survivors experience long-term functional limitations and reduced quality of life (QoL). Reperfusion strategies can rapidly relieve right-ventricular (RV) dysfunction and prevent clinical deterioration or hemodynamic collapse; however, these approaches have never been evaluated in a randomized trial against anticoagulation alone using patient-centered outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate whether mechanical thrombectomy with anticoagulation improves functional, QoL, and safety outcomes compared with anticoagulation alone in patients with acute intermediate-high risk PE over 90 days. METHODS: STORM-PE enrolled 100 PE patients randomized 1:1 to computer-assisted vacuum thrombectomy (CAVT) with anticoagulation or anticoagulation alone across 22 international sites, with RV-to-left-ventricular (RV/LV) ratio change at 48 hours as the primary endpoint. Secondary endpoints included major adverse events within 7 days, functional and QoL outcomes, mortality, and symptomatic PE recurrence through 90 days. RESULTS: For all patients, median time from randomization to last follow-up visit was 91.0 days [Q1-Q3: 80.5-100.0]. At 90 days, 66.0% (31/47) of CAVT and 64.2% (34/53) of anticoagulation patients completed the 6-min walk test. The CAVT arm exhibited a longer 6-min walk distance compared with anticoagulation alone (478.7 ± 159.5 m vs 368.0 ± 127.8 m, P = 0.003). More CAVT than anticoagulation patients were NYHA functional class I (97.4% [37/38] vs 75.6% [34/45], P = 0.005) at 90 days. Dyspnea and QoL scores were comparable between groups, with no differences between arms for all-cause mortality, PE-related mortality, and symptomatic PE recurrence within 90 days. CONCLUSIONS: In STORM-PE, CAVT with anticoagulation resulted in improved functional outcomes at 90 days compared with anticoagulation alone, with equivalent safety rates. This trial supports CAVT as an effective and safe reperfusion strategy for intermediate-high risk PE. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov Unique Identifier: NCT05684796.

title: Occlusion-Focused Triage vs Very-High-Risk NSTEMI Criteria
abstract: Background The current ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)/NSTEMI framework may not fully identify patients with ACO who present without diagnostic STE. Although immediate invasive management is recommended for patients with very-high-risk NSTEMI features, these criteria are inconsistently applied in clinical practice. The OMI/NOMI framework has been proposed as an alternative strategy. Objectives This study sought to compare the occlusive and nonocclusive myocardial infarction (OMI/NOMI) classification with guideline-defined very-high-risk non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) criteria for the identification of acute coronary occlusion (ACO) in patients without diagnostic STE. Methods This was a substudy of the multicenter, cluster-randomized DIFOCCULT-3 (Time for a Diagnostic Paradigm Shift From ST-Elevation/Non-ST-Elevation to Occlusion/Non-Occlusion Myocardial Infarction-3) trial. Consecutive adult patients without diagnostic STE on the admission electrocardiogram were included and managed according to either the conventional STEMI/NSTEMI or the OMI/NOMI approach. Very-high-risk NSTEMI was defined according to current guidelines. Outcomes included immediate invasive management (within 2 hours) and adjudicated ACO. Results Among 4,398 patients, very-high-risk NSTEMI criteria identified a small proportion of patients and were inconsistently translated into early intervention. The OMI/NOMI approach selected more patients for early invasive management compared with the STEMI/NSTEMI framework (45.4% vs 13.6%; P Conclusions An occlusion-focused diagnostic approach was associated with substantially higher rates of immediate invasive management and earlier identification of patients with adjudicated ACO.

abstract: Background Patients may present with acute coronary occlusions (ACOs) without manifesting electrocardiographic criteria for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Objectives The aim of this study was to examine the incidence, clinical characteristics, and in-hospital outcomes of non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) with ACO. Methods The study included patients with STEMI and NSTEMI in the CathPCI Registry who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention between April 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023. ACO was defined as 100% stenosis deemed acute. The cohort was stratified into STEMI (including STEMI equivalents), NSTEMI-ACO, and NSTEMI-no-ACO. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular mortality. A sensitivity analysis with ACO defined as 100% acute occlusion or TIMI flow grade 0 or 1 in the culprit artery was performed. Results Of 1,198,544 patients, 26.1% had STEMI, 11.0% had NSTEMI-ACO (15% of whom had NSTEMI), and 62.9% had NSTEMI-no-ACO. Compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO, NSTEMI-ACO patients had more cardiogenic shock (9.0% STEMI vs 3.8% NSTEMI-ACO vs 1.9% NSTEMI-no-ACO; P Conclusions ACO occurs in a substantial proportion of patients with NSTEMI and is associated with worse in-hospital outcomes relative to those with NSTEMI-no-ACO. Further studies of early identification and reperfusion practices for NSTEMI-ACO are warranted.

title: Immediate Versus Staged Complete Revascularization in Multivessel Disease and STEMI
abstract: Background For patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel disease, complete revascularization is recommended. The timing of nonculprit lesion intervention, either immediately during the index procedure or staged at a later time, has been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Objectives This study sought to perform a meta-analysis of RCTs comparing immediate vs staged complete revascularization in patients with multivessel disease presenting with STEMI. Methods We conducted a frequentist, pairwise meta-analysis. Studies were selected based on the following inclusion criteria: multicenter RCTs comparing immediate vs staged nonculprit revascularization in patients presenting with STEMI; exclusive use of second-generation (or newer) drug-eluting stents; a follow-up duration of ≥1 year; and publication in a peer-reviewed journal. The primary outcome of interest was all-cause mortality, whereas secondary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), cardiac death, and unplanned revascularization. Summary estimates were computed using random-effects models with inverse-variance weighting based on trial-level HRs and 95% CIs. The study protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251124207). Results After a systematic search, 4 randomized trials comprising 2,651 patients were included in the meta-analysis. The risk of all-cause death at 1-year was higher with immediate complete revascularization (HR: 1.50; 95% CI: 1.02-2.21; P = 0.04; prediction interval [PI]: 0.80-2.81; I 2 = 0%; t 2 = 0). Immediate complete revascularization reduced the risk of recurrent MI when using the protocol specified definitions which included procedural MI (HR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.36-0.94; P = 0.02; PI: 0.22-1.54; I 2 = 0%; t 2 = 0.034) but did not reduce risk of spontaneous MI (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.55-1.48; P = 0.90; PI: 0.41-2.00; I 2 = 0%; τ 2 = 0.00). The risk of cardiac death and unplanned revascularization was comparable between the treatment groups. Conclusions In STEMI and multivessel disease, immediate complete revascularization may be associated with an increased risk of all-cause death at 1-year when compared with staged complete revascularization. The treatment effect on mortality should be interpreted cautiously because of the relatively low number of deaths across the 4 trials and the statistical fragility of the findings. The findings from this analysis do not support an immediate complete revascularization strategy in these patients.

title: Impact of Extent of Coronary Artery Disease in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement
abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease is present in one-half of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The recent randomized controlled PRO-TAVI (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial indicated that deferral of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is safe in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease at 1-year follow-up. The SYNTAX (Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery) score quantifies the extent of coronary artery disease, which may guide individualized revascularization strategies. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between SYNTAX score (SS) and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TAVR. METHODS: This study was a substudy of the PRO-TAVI trial, including 466 patients with significant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR randomized to deferral of PCI or PCI before TAVR. SS was calculated from preprocedural coronary angiograms, and patients were stratified by SS quartiles. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and major bleeding at 1 year. An ischemic composite outcome of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and stroke was also assessed. RESULTS: The primary composite outcome did not differ across SS categories between the deferral and PCI groups at 1-year follow-up, which was completed by all but 1 patient. In patients with SS >17, the ischemic composite outcome occurred more often in the deferral group (30.9% vs 14.8%; adjusted HR: 2.43; 95% CI: 1.04-5.64; P = 0.04), driven primarily by all-cause mortality and stroke. Bleeding events were less frequent in the deferral group across all SS subgroups. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with concomitant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR, deferral of PCI reduced bleeding risk and appeared safe across all SS categories. Deferral of PCI in patients with more complex coronary artery disease (SS >17) was associated with higher risk for the ischemic composite outcome. These post hoc findings require confirmation in randomized trials. (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation [PRO-TAVI]; NCT05078619).

title: Intraprocedural Cardiac Arrest in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Interventions in the United States
abstract: Background Cardiac arrest (CA) during percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) is a catastrophic procedural complication. Contemporary rates of CA during PCI are unknown. Objectives This study sought to understand contemporary rates of CA, associated mortality, and identify predictors of CA during PCI. Methods Patients with CA during PCI from 2018 to 2023 were identified from the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI Registry. Trends in intraprocedural CA (IPCA) incidence and in-hospital death were evaluated. Predictors of IPCA and risk-adjusted mortality were identified. Results A total of 36,755 IPCA occurred during 3,956,840 PCIs (0.93%), including in 0.24% of elective PCIs, 0.32% of PCIs for stable coronary artery disease, and 1.28% of acute coronary syndrome interventions. The incidence of IPCA increased over time (0.62% in 2018 to 1.07% in 2023; P Conclusions IPCA complicates 0.93% of contemporary PCI. Despite an increasing incidence of risk-adjusted IPCA, there were slight declines in risk-adjusted in-hospital mortality in the study period. Several patient and procedural characteristics were independently associated with intraprocedural CA.

Frequency and Prognosis of Alternative Definitions of Occlusion Myocardial Infarction Across the Whole Spectrum of Acute Coronary Syndromes
authors: Jose Maria De La Torre Hernandez
abstract: Background Occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) refers to a myocardial infarction caused by a persistent or transient, complete or near-complete coronary artery occlusion. Multiple definitions have been proposed, yet their frequency and comparative prognostic relevance remain unclear. Objectives This study sought to evaluate the frequency and prognosis of previously proposed OMI definitions across the whole spectrum of acute coronary syndromes (ACS) from the MATRIX trial. Methods Five alternative OMI definitions were assessed: 1) culprit artery (CA) TIMI flow grade 0; 2) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-1; 3) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2; 4) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2 or TIMI flow grade 3 with cardiac troponin >30× upper reference limit; and 5) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2 or CA-TIMI flow grade 3 with cardiac troponin >100× upper reference limit. The endpoint of interest was 1-year all-cause mortality. Results Among 6,558 patients with ACS, OMI frequency ranged from 37.8% for definition 1 to 76.1% for definition 4. OMI was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality according to definitions 1-4 (adjusted HR: 2.08 [95% CI: 1.56-2.78], 1.97[1.47-2.63], 1.70 [1.25-2.32], 1.47 [1.01-2.12], respectively) but not according to definition 5 (adjusted HR: 1.26 [0.90-1.75]). OMI definitions exclusively based on impaired CA flow (ie, definitions 1-3) improved discrimination, reclassification, and model fit when added to the conventional STE/NSTE-ACS classification. One-year mortality did not differ among patients with NSTE-ACS with OMI definition 1 or 2 compared with ST-segment elevation MI (STEMI) patients. Conclusions OMI defined by impaired CA flow confers prognostic implications beyond the presence or absence of ST-segment elevation in a broad ACS population and identifies patients without ST-segment elevation with 1-year mortality similar to that of STEMI.

title: Conduction System Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Patients Undergoing TAVR
abstract: Background Pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac physiological pacing (CPP) may preserve ventricular synchrony and reduce heart failure (HF) events compared with right ventricular pacing (RVP). Objectives This study sought to compare long-term clinical outcomes of CPP vs RVP in patients requiring permanent pacing after TAVR. Methods Registro de Estimulación Fisiológica-TAVR is a retrospective, multicenter nationwide registry including patients undergoing TAVR and pacemaker implantation within 30 days. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using baseline clinical and echocardiographic variables, yielding 466 matched pairs. The primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization. Cox proportional hazards models were used for time-to-event analyses. Median follow-up was 24 months. Results In the propensity score-matched cohort, CPP was associated with a lower incidence of the primary endpoint than RVP (9.7% vs 17.6%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.39-0.83; P = 0.003). This difference was driven by fewer HF hospitalizations (7.9% vs 13.9%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.37-0.86; P = 0.008). No significant differences were observed in cardiovascular death or all-cause mortality between groups. Conclusions In this multicenter propensity score-matched study, CPP after TAVR was associated with a lower risk of the primary endpoint, driven by fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support the need for further randomized clinical trials to evaluate the role of CPP in post-TAVR patients requiring ventricular pacing.

abstract: BACKGROUND: The clinical utility of optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) for guiding endovascular therapy in femoropopliteal lesions has not been established. Additionally, the prognostic value of OFDI findings during drug-coated balloon (DCB) treatment for femoropopliteal lesions has never been evaluated. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to clarify the feasibility of OFDI-guided DCB treatment and investigate the OFDI findings associated with restenosis after DCB treatment in femoropopliteal lesions. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, observational study included patients with symptomatic, nonseverely calcified femoropopliteal lesions who underwent DCB treatment under OFDI guidance. Procedural success was defined as residual stenosis of less than 30% without flow compromise and without any procedural complications. The primary outcome was restenosis of the target lesion, defined as a peak systolic velocity ratio of ≥2.5, as measured by duplex ultrasound at rest or target lesion revascularization. RESULTS: A total of 202 lesions were initially enrolled, of which 35 (17.3%) were excluded primarily because of severe calcification or inadequate OFDI data. Among the 167 analyzable lesions included in the present analysis, the procedural success rate and 1-year freedom from restenosis were 91.6% and 85.5%, respectively. In the procedural OFDI findings, a calcified nodule in the target lesion (subdistribution hazard ratio: 3.25; 95% CI: 1.01-10.42; P = 0.048) was associated with restenosis. CONCLUSIONS: OFDI-guided DCB treatment is feasible in selected femoropopliteal lesions. An OFDI-detected calcified nodule is associated with an increased risk of restenosis after DCB treatment for femoropopliteal lesions.

abstract: Background Whether age affects the comparative treatment effect of immediate complete revascularization (CR) vs staged CR during the index admission in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease remains unknown. Objectives This study aimed to assess how age influences clinical outcomes in patients with with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. Methods This is a secondary analysis of the OPTION-STEMI (Optimal Timing of Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided Complete Revascularization for Non-Infarct-Related Artery in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction with Multivessel Disease) trial, which included 994 patients randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. The primary endpoint at 1 year, defined as a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or any unplanned revascularization, was analyzed according to age and CR strategy. Results A significant interaction was found between age, as a continuous variable, and CR strategy for the primary endpoint (interaction P = 0.015). The HR for the primary endpoint was initially higher in the staged CR arm until approximately 67 years, after which it increased steadily in the immediate CR arm. In the binary analysis, a significantly higher incidence of the primary endpoint was observed in the immediate CR arm compared with the staged CR arm in patients ≥70 years (45 of 202 [22.3%] vs 29 of 210 [13.8%]; HR: 1.68; 95% CI: 1.06-2.69; log-rank P = 0.029), but not in patients Conclusions This post hoc analysis of the OPTION-STEMI trial demonstrates that older patients experience significantly worse clinical outcomes with immediate CR than with in-hospital staged CR. These findings suggest that age modifies the treatment effect of the CR strategy and warrant confirmation in adequately powered trials (Timing of FFR-guided PCI for Non-IRA in STEMI and MVD [OPTION-STEMI]; NCT04626882).

abstract: Background Residual mitral regurgitation (MR) after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is a major determinant of outcome. However, the prognostic impact of recurrent mitral regurgitation (recMR) after initially successful M-TEER remains unclear. Objectives This study aimed to evaluate the association between recMR after successful M-TEER and long-term mortality across degenerative mitral regurgitation (DMR) and functional mitral regurgitation (FMR). Methods This retrospective cohort included 461 consecutive patients with MR undergoing successful M-TEER (residual mitral regurgitation ≤2+ at discharge) between 2008 and 2021. recMR was defined as ≥1-grade increase in mitral regurgitation severity at follow-up compared with discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Results Among 461 patients with MR undergoing M_TEER (mean age 75.0 ± 9.1 years; 60.7% male [280 of 461]; 29.3% [135 of 461] had DMR), recMR occurred in 31.7% (146 of 461) (FMR in 31.9% [104 of 326]; DMR in 31.1% [42 of 135]). The median follow-up time was 3.44 years (Q1-Q3: 1.51-3.99 years). In a 12-month landmark analysis, absence of recMR was associated with improved survival (log-rank, P = 0.0088). At 4 years, all-cause mortality was 44.8% (95% CI: 38.7%-50.3%) in patients without recMR and 56.3% (95% CI: 47.2%-63.9%) in those with recMR. In multivariable Cox regression, recMR independently predicted higher mortality (HR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.06-1.93; P = 0.019). The survival difference was significant in patients with DMR (log-rank, P = 0.014) but not with FMR (P = 0.11). Conclusions recMR is common and independently associated with increased mortality after M-TEER, with a more pronounced effect in patients with DMR. Identification of patients at risk may inform closer surveillance and timely reintervention.

title: Dynamic Common Iliac Vein Compression by the Adjacent Intestine Revealed by Intravascular Ultrasound

abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) uses ultrasonic acoustic pressure waves to modify calcification to enable optimal balloon and stent expansion in calcified lesions. However, the dose-response relationship for creating fractures within calcified lesions of different calcium morphologies is unknown. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the dose-dependent effects of IVL on calcium fracture overall and in the setting of calcification arc <180° vs ≥180°. METHODS: Micro-computed tomography images were acquired before and after 10, 20, 40, 60, 80, and 120 pulses of IVL treatment (Shockwave Medical) in an ex vivo study of 5 cadaveric human hearts (15 coronary lesions). A total of 30 cross-sections of micro-computed tomography (2 sections per lesion) were analyzed for this study. RESULTS: Cumulative fracture occurrence increased progressively with the number of IVL pulses delivered, with fractures observed in 33% of sections after 10 pulses, 50% after 40 pulses, and 60% after 120 pulses. Calcification arc ≥180° exhibited a higher fracture occurrence compared with arc <180° (P = 0.028). After adjustment for pulse number, calcification arc ≥180° was associated with significantly higher fracture counts compared with arc <180° (rate ratio = 6.1, P = 0.003). CONCLUSIONS: Fracture occurrence following IVL increased with cumulative pulse delivery and differed significantly according to calcification concentricity. Calcification arc ≥180° demonstrated a higher and earlier likelihood of fracture occurrence than arc <180°, independent of pulse number. These findings establish a clear dose-dependent relationship between IVL pulse delivery and fracture formation and highlight calcification concentricity as a key determinant of fracture response.

abstract: Background Over 70% of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) present with below-the-knee disease, and there is a growing trend towards endovascular revascularization. Objectives The Dutch Chronic Lower Limb-Threatening Ischemia Registry (THRILLER) aimed to provide real-world data on outcomes after popliteal and infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization to guide revascularization strategies. Methods This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals. Primary outcomes were limb salvage and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 24 months, estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Results Between February 2021 and December 2023, a total of 1,119 interventions in 1,060 limbs (938 patients) were included, treating 551 popliteal, 1,352 tibial, and 239 pedal lesions. The median follow-up was 43.6 months (Q1-Q3: 35.5-52.7 months). Technical success was achieved in 92.3% (1,033/1,119). Limb salvage and AFS decreased significantly after technical failure and with increasing WIfI stage and Rutherford category. Compared to Rutherford 5, Rutherford 6 limbs had significantly worse limb salvage (HR: 3.07; 95% CI: 1.89-4.99; P Conclusions Endovascular revascularization for popliteal and infrapopliteal disease in patients with CLTI is safe and effective in preventing limb loss and mortality at 2 years, although patients with Rutherford 6 limbs face significantly worse outcomes, particularly in the first 3 months.

title: Calcium Fracture Detection by Optical Coherence Tomography Versus Intravascular Ultrasound Following Intravascular Lithotripsy
abstract: BACKGROUND: Calcium fracture is a metric used to assess lesion preparation success. We have shown previously that optical coherence tomography (OCT) misses approximately half of these fractures. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) is the most commonly used intravascular imaging modality. The sensitivity of IVUS for detecting calcium fractures after intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is unknown. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to assess the frequency and characteristics of calcium fracture observed on IVUS in comparison to OCT and gold standard micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) using heavily calcified coronary artery cadaveric vessels. METHODS: In an ex vivo study of 5 cadaveric hearts (15 coronary lesions), OCT, IVUS, and micro-CT were obtained before and after IVL coronary artery treatment. Fracture detection rates and appearance patterns were compared across modalities. Receiver operating characteristic analyses evaluated OCT-measured fracture width thresholds for IVUS detectability. RESULTS: Compared with micro-CT, OCT and IVUS significantly underestimated fracture occurrence, but OCT demonstrated higher detection sensitivity than IVUS (P < 0.05 by McNemar's test). Narrow linear nondisplaced fractures identified on OCT were frequently undetectable on IVUS or appeared as subtle hyperechoic shadows. Fracture width was strongly associated with IVUS detectability; fracture width >115 μm on OCT were identified by IVUS with excellent diagnostic performance (area under the curve: 0.99 [95% CI: 0.98-1.00], sensitivity 100%, specificity 92%). CONCLUSIONS: OCT and IVUS underestimate the occurrence of IVL-induced calcium fractures compared with micro-CT, with IVUS demonstrating lower sensitivity than OCT. IVUS detectability is strongly dependent on fracture width. Absence of visible fracture on either OCT or IVUS does not exclude calcium modification.

title: Beyond Procedural Success
Periprocedural Pulmonary Hypertension and Outcomes After Mitral Valve Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair
abstract: Background Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is common in patients undergoing mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER), but the prognostic significance of periprocedural PH changes remains uncertain. Objectives This study sought to evaluate the association between periprocedural PH patterns and clinical outcomes after M-TEER and to identify predictors of residual and new-onset PH. Methods The OCEAN-Mitral registry prospectively enrolled 3,764 patients with severe mitral regurgitation treated with M-TEER. Among 3,484 patients with paired echocardiographic tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) data, PH was defined as TRPG >31 mm Hg. Patients were classified as having no PH, normalized PH, new-onset PH, or residual PH according to pre- and postprocedural PH status. The primary endpoint was 2-year cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of residual and new-onset PH. Results No PH was observed in 1,432 patients (41.1%), normalized PH in 763 (21.9%), new-onset PH in 298 (8.6%), and residual PH in 991 (28.4%). The 2-year incidence of the primary endpoint differed significantly across groups (17.6%, 18.1%, 27.2%, and 27.6%, respectively; P 50 mm Hg, and tricuspid annular dilation predicted residual PH, whereas residual mitral regurgitation and postprocedural transmitral gradients >5 mm Hg predicted new-onset PH. Conclusions Periprocedural PH dynamics provide robust risk stratification after M-TEER, identifying low-risk patients with PH normalization and high-risk subsets with residual or new-onset PH, requiring closer surveillance and procedural optimization. Registration Treatment and Prognosis of Heart Valve Registry; UMIN-ID: UMIN000023653.

title: Safety and Effectiveness of a Novel Laser-Based Intravascular Lithotripsy System for Coronary Calcium
abstract: ObjectivesThis study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of a novel laser- and optic-based quad-emitter IVL system in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions. MethodsFRACTURE was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm trial. The primary safety endpoint was 30-day freedom from major adverse cardiac events (MACE; composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, or target vessel revascularization). The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success (successful stent delivery with a final residual stenosis <50% and freedom from in-hospital MACE). Both endpoints were evaluated against prespecified performance goals. An optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy was performed. ResultsA total of 420 patients (mean age: 71.2 ± 9.01 years; 74.0% male) were enrolled. Median calcified length was 34.4 mm (Q1-Q3: 21.3-52.5 mm). Among 106 patients with OCT, at the site of maximum calcification, the calcium arc was 271.89° ± 77.35° and the median thickness was 0.88 mm (Q1-Q3: 0.72-1.11 mm). OCT confirmed calcium fracture in 67% of lesions; the median minimal stent area was 6.51 mm2 (Q1-Q3: 4.85-7.78 mm2), and stent expansion was 94.2% ± 19.4% at the site of maximum calcification. The primary safety endpoint of 30-day freedom from MACE was 93.3% (373/400; with lower bound of 95% CI of 90.8%, exceeding the 86.2% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). The primary effectiveness endpoint of procedural success was 93.7% (374/399; with lower bound of 95% CI of 91.3%, exceeding the 85.8% performance goal [P < 0.0001]). ConclusionsThe quad-emitter IVL system is a safe and effective option to modify severe calcified coronary lesions and facilitate stent implantation. Registration: (Modification of Coronary Calcium With Laser Based Intravascular Lithotripsy for Coronary Artery Disease [FRACTURE]; NCT06181240)

Sirolimus- Versus Everolimus-Eluting Stents With Contemporary PCI in Three-Vessel Disease: The Multivessel TALENT Randomized Noninferiority Trial
authors: Jose M. De la Torre Hernandez
abstract: Background Contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has improved outcomes in three-vessel disease (3VD). However, the Supraflex Cruz sirolimus-eluting stent (SES) has not been compared with the SYNERGY everolimus-eluting stent (EES) in this setting. Objectives We compared the performance of the Supraflex Cruz SES and the SYNERGY EES in patients with de novo 3VD undergoing contemporary PCI. Methods We randomized 1,548 patients to the Supraflex Cruz SES (n=774) or the SYNERGY EES (n=774). Patients were selected after Heart Team discussion incorporating the SYNTAX Score II. Contemporary PCI included angiography-derived physiology, intravascular imaging optimization, CTO expertise, and short DAPT followed by prasugrel monotherapy. The primary endpoint was the 1-year patient-oriented composite endpoint (POCE: all-cause death, any stroke, any myocardial infarction, or any revascularization), estimated by Kaplan–Meier in the intention-to-treat population. The non-inferiority margin was 4.28%. Results Median follow-up was 367 days (IQR, 362–372). At 1 year, POCE was 15.23% (95% CI, 12.87–17.96) with Supraflex Cruz SES and 14.51% (95% CI, 12.20–17.21) with SYNERGY EES. The risk difference was 0.72 percentage points; the one-sided 95% upper confidence bound was 3.71%, below the margin (P non-inferiority=0.025). Myocardial infarction occurred in 10.07% (95% CI, 8.14–12.43) versus 8.14% (95% CI, 6.41–10.33), revascularization in 6.40% (95% CI, 4.86–8.40) versus 6.81% (95% CI, 5.22–8.87), and stent thrombosis in 1.31% (95% CI, 0.71–2.43) versus 1.08% (95% CI, 0.54–2.14). Conclusions In patients with 3VD undergoing contemporary PCI, the Supraflex Cruz SES was noninferior to the SYNERGY EES for 1-year POCE. Clinical Trial Registration NCT04390672

title: Fully Retrievable Self-Expanding Short-Frame Valve for Aortic Regurgitation
Prognostic Impact of Discharge Transprosthetic Tricuspid Gradient After Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement
abstract: Background Although transprosthetic gradients are established prognostic markers after left-sided valve interventions, the prognostic significance of discharge tricuspid gradient (dTVG) after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) remains unclear. Objectives This study sought to evaluate the association between dTVG and clinical outcomes after TTVR and identify high dTVG determinants. Methods TRIPLACE (Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement) is an international, multicenter TTVR registry. A discharge landmark analysis was performed, excluding patients with in-hospital mortality, lack of TTVR technical success, missing dTVG, or unavailable follow-up at any time point. Endpoints included all-cause mortality and the composite of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. The optimal dTVG cutoff was identified through quartile-based survival analysis and confirmed by log-rank maximization. Multivariable Cox models were developed using cross-validated candidate variable selection. Results Among 526 patients, 474 were included. Median follow-up was 208.5 days (Q1-Q3: 54-474 days). A data-driven dTVG cutoff of 3.5 mm Hg identified 122 of 474 patients (25.7%) with high dTVG. dTVG ≥3.5 mm Hg was associated with higher 1- and 3-year mortality (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.14-3.75; P = 0.017 and HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.24-3.48; P = 0.006, respectively) and composite endpoint events (HR: 1.99; 95% CI: 1.31-3.03; P = 0.001 and HR: 1.96; 95% CI: 1.33-2.88; P 2 increase; 95% CI: 0.71-0.88). Conclusions Elevated dTVG after TTVR independently identifies patients at increased risk of adverse outcomes. A 3.5 mm Hg threshold may support postprocedural risk stratification, whereas inner valve diameter represents a potentially modifiable determinant of elevated dTVG. (TRIPLACE [Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement]; NCT06033274).

title: One Lesion, Two Perspectives
Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve-in-Valve and Valve-in-Ring Implantation: the TRIVIR registry
abstract: Background Transcatheter tricuspid valve-in-valve (TViV) and valve-in-ring (TViR) procedures are increasingly used; however, data on clinical outcomes, valve performance, and symptomatic improvement remain limited. Objectives To evaluate a real-world multicenter cohort undergoing transcatheter TViV and TViR procedures. Methods We conducted an international multicenter registry including patients undergoing TViV/TViR procedures. The TRIVIR Registry evaluated all-cause mortality and a composite endpoint (CE), defined as all-cause mortality, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and tricuspid bioprosthesis degeneration during follow-up. Results Between 2012 and 2025, 75 patients underwent TViV (n=62) or TViR (n=13) across 16 centers using Sapien (88%) or Myval (12%) valves. Median follow up was 1.86 years (IQR 0.10-2.59). Mean age was 62±13 years, and 69% were women. NYHA class III–IV decreased from 72% at baseline to 13% at 1-3 months and remained low during follow-up. No 30-day deaths occurred, while periprocedural complications occurred in 24% of procedures, mostly minor (17.3%). At 3 years, the Kaplan–Meier estimates of all-cause mortality and CE were 35.6% and 42.9%, and the cumulative incidences of HF hospitalization and tricuspid bioprosthesis degeneration were 16.6% and 11.4%, respectively. Patients who died had markers of advanced disease, including higher NT-proBNP levels, greater diuretic requirements, more frequent pacing/CRT implantation, and higher procedural complication rates. Conclusions TViV/TViR represents a viable treatment strategy and provided sustained symptomatic improvement in high-risk patients. Patients who died exhibited a more advanced clinical profile, highlighting the importance of appropriate patient selection, early referral, and treatment in experienced centers.

Thirty-Day Outcomes of a Dedicated Transcatheter Occlusion Device for Paravalvular Leak Closure: The PARADIGM Study
abstract: BACKGROUND Paravalvular leak (PVL) is a complication of surgical valve replacement and is associated with poor prognosis. Percutaneous device closure offers a less invasive alternative to repeat surgery. OBJECTIVE Evaluate the Amplatzer Valvular Plug III (APVL3) for PVL closure after surgical implant of a mechanical or bioprosthetic valve. METHODS PARADIGM is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study assessing transcatheter PVL closure. The primary endpoint was a composite of safety and effectiveness measures evaluating the implant success, PVL reduction ≥2 grades on exit from the procedure, procedural mortality, and device-related reinterventions through 30 days. Descriptive safety and performance endpoints were evaluated at 30 days. RESULTS A total of 200 patients were enrolled across 24 sites in the United States, Europe, and Canada. Average age was 67.7+/-11.5 years, 58.5% were male, and 70.0% had a mechanical valve. Median(IQR) logistic EuroSCORE was 5.2(3.2,10.3), median(IQR) STS PROM was 2.9%(1.4,5.4), and 53.1%(104/196) were NYHA class III/IV. Heart failure was the primary indication for PVL closure (89.5%), and 65.0% were treated for mitral PVL. Successful implantation was achieved in 96.0%(192/200), with no procedural mortality. The primary endpoint was met in 94.0%(188/200), exceeding the performance goal(P<0.0001). The 30-day procedural success was 77.3%(140/181). At 30 days, mortality was 2.0%(4/200,95%CI:0.5-5.0), hemolytic anemia occurred in 3.5%(7/200,95% CI:1.42%,7.08%), 95.7%(156/163) had mild or less PVL, 82.7%(143/173) were NYHA class I/II, and KCCQ-OS improved by 15.7(12.6,18.8) points. CONCLUSION PARADIGM met its primary endpoint, with favorable short-term outcomes. The results support this transcatheter device as a promising therapeutic option for PVL closure. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04489823

title: Posterior Leaflet Restoration for Secondary Mitral Regurgitation
abstract: BACKGROUND: Secondary mitral regurgitation (MR) contributes to morbidity and mortality in patients with symptomatic valve disease. Although transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is beneficial, many patients remain suboptimal candidates. Posterior leaflet restoration (PLR) provides a prosthetic coaptation surface via an adaptive coaptation element that inflates during systole and deflates during diastole to facilitate leaflet coaptation. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the safety and feasibility of PLR using the MRace implant (Polares Medical, Inc). METHODS: Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant in Georgia and Brazil (EXPLORE MR) enrolled 78 symptomatic patients with severe secondary MR (≥3+), stratified post hoc by left ventricular end-diastolic volume: nonseverely enlarged left ventricle (NSELV) (N = 46) and severely enlarged left ventricle (SELV) (N = 32). The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality; secondary endpoints were MR reduction and functional outcomes. RESULTS: The implant was successfully deployed in 96.2% of patients. All-cause mortality at 30 days was 6.4%. MR ≤2+ was achieved in 93.8% of patients at 30 days and was sustained in 90.6% at 1 year. Patients with NSELV showed better results in MR ≤1+ at every time point (94.4% at 30 days, 89.5% at 1 year) compared with the SELV group (79.3% and 69.2%, respectively). The NSELV subgroup demonstrated better functional recovery, with NYHA functional class I or II rising from 8.7% to 84.2%, vs a more attenuated response in the SELV group (15.6%-76.9%). The 6-minute walk test improved in the paired NSELV cohort (Δ +93.9 m), but not in paired patients with SELV (Δ -7.8 m). Kaplan-Meier 1-year all-cause mortality was 29.5% overall and was better in patients with NSELV (19.4%) than in SELV (41.7%). CONCLUSIONS: PLR with the MRace implant achieves substantial MR reduction and meaningful functional improvement, most pronounced in patients without severely enlarged left ventricles. (XPLORE MRace [BR]: Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant [EXPLORE MRace]; NCT06113354).

title: TECTONIC CAD
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe coronary calcification complicates percutaneous coronary intervention by limiting lesion compliance and impairing stent expansion. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the SonicForce Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy System (Abbott Vascular) in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions. METHODS: TECTONIC CAD intravascular lithotripsy investigational device exemption (NCT06885177) was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study of 335 patients at 40 U.S. CENTERS: The primary safety endpoint was 30-day target lesion failure, defined as cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success. Each endpoint was tested against a prespecified performance goal. A prespecified optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy evaluated calcium modification and stent expansion. RESULTS: , with stent expansion of 95.9% ± 18.6%. Calcium fracture was identified in 62.5% (50 of 80) of lesions after intravascular lithotripsy and 66.3% (53 of 80) after stenting. CONCLUSIONS: TECTONIC CAD met both prespecified coprimary safety and effectiveness endpoints, demonstrating low 30-day target lesion failure and high procedural success. OCT demonstrated calcium fracture and favorable stent expansion at maximum contiguous calcium.

title: Rotational Atherectomy Plus Intravascular Lithotripsy Versus Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone for Coronary Calcified Nodules
abstract: Background Optimal lesion preparation for coronary calcified nodules (CNs) and intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) pulse delivery for severe calcification remain uncertain. Objectives This study sought to evaluate phenotype-specific calcium modification in severe calcification with and without CNs. Methods In this single-center randomized trial using a new-generation coronary IVL catheter, patients with optical coherence tomography-defined CNs (Cohort A) were assigned 1:1 to rotational atherectomy (RA) plus IVL or IVL alone; patients with severe calcification without CNs (Cohort B) were assigned 1:1 to maximum or operator-determined IVL pulses. Primary endpoints were minimum stent area (MSA) at the CN site in Cohort A and at the maximum calcium arc site in Cohort B. Results Among 120 patients, 66 (55%) were in Cohort A (33 per group) and 54 (45%) in Cohort B (27 per group). MSA at the CN site was 7.41 ± 2.12 mm 2 with RA plus IVL vs 6.23 ± 1.55 mm 2 with IVL alone (mean difference: 1.18 mm 2 ; 95% CI: 0.27-2.09; P = 0.012). In Cohort B, MSA at the maximum calcium arc site was 5.50 ± 1.19 mm 2 with maximum IVL pulses vs 5.56 ± 1.45 mm 2 with operator-determined IVL pulses (mean difference: -0.06 mm 2 ; 95% CI: -0.78 to 0.67; P = 0.873). Conclusions RA plus IVL increased final stent area vs IVL alone in CN lesions, whereas maximum IVL pulses did not significantly increase final stent area compared with operator-determined pulses in severe calcification without CNs. These findings warrant validation in larger multicenter trials with clinical endpoints. (Coronary Calcified Nodule Management With Rotational Atherectomy Plus Shockwave Intravascular Lithotripsy vs Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone: A Prospective, Randomized Trial [NODULE-SHOCK]; ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07000045).

title: 1-Year Safety and Effectiveness of a Next-Generation Dual-Seal Left Atrial Appendage Occluder
abstract: BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is a stroke prevention alternative for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) intolerant to long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC). The next-generation dual-seal device was designed to improve operator ease of use while maintaining effective LAAO of the predicate device. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this analysis was to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a next-generation device through 1 year. METHODS: VERITAS is a single-arm, prospective, global, multicenter study. Patients with nonvalvular AF with an increased thromboembolism risk seeking a nonpharmacologic alternative to OAC were enrolled. One-year descriptive endpoints are provided, including mortality, neurological events, major bleeding, and device-related complications. One-year cardiac imaging was assessed for peridevice leak and device-related thrombus (DRT). RESULTS: Complete left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (0 mm leak) was observed in 91.1% (95% CI: 87.9%-93.7%) of patients by either transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) or cardiac computed tomography and 96.3% (95% CI: 93.2%-98.2%) by TEE alone. The cumulative DRT rate was 3.3% (95% CI: 2.0%-5.3%) with only 0.4% (95% CI: 0.1%-1.5%) deemed clinically relevant. One-year key clinical outcome rates are as follows: all-cause mortality: 3.9% (95% CI: 2.4%-6.3%); cardiovascular mortality: 1.9% (95% CI: 0.9%-3.8%); major bleeding: 6.6% (95% CI: 4.5%-9.2%); ischemic stroke or systemic embolism: 1.8% (95% CI: 0.8%-3.3%); pericardial effusion requiring intervention: 0.9% (95% CI: 0.3%-2.1%). No (0%) device embolization occurred. Median follow-up was 365 days (IQR: 349-380 days). CONCLUSIONS: The VERITAS study results support the 1-year safety and effectiveness of the next-generation device. (Abbott Medical-VERITAS Study; NCT06707688).

title: 3-Year Comparison of Sirolimus- Versus Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Femoropopliteal Artery Disease
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sirolimus-coated balloons (SCBs) have emerged as alternatives to paclitaxel-coated balloons (PCBs), but randomized comparative data beyond 2 years are lacking. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient-reported outcomes, effectiveness, and safety through 3 years in symptomatic femoropopliteal artery disease. METHODS: SIRONA was a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial comparing SCB angioplasty with a PCB strategy. Patients were randomized 1:1 after successful predilation. Prespecified 3-year outcomes included walking capacity, health-related quality of life, clinically driven target lesion/vessel revascularization (cdTLR/cdTVR), mortality, major amputation, and amputation-free survival. RESULTS: Among 482 randomized patients (SCB, n = 238; PCB, n = 244), 96.3% had intermittent claudication; 3-year follow-up was completed by 76.5% and 79.6%, respectively. Changes in patient-reported walking distances did not differ between-groups. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was 88.2% (95% CI: 83.1%-91.9%) versus 80.2% (95% CI: 74.1%-85.0%; HR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.36-0.97; nominal log-rank P = 0.03). Post-hoc analysis suggested time-varying treatment effects (treatment-by-period interaction P = 0.006), with separation after the first year. Freedom from cdTVR (HR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.50-1.21; nominal P = 0.27) and amputation-free survival (HR: 1.09, 95% CI 0.57-2.09; nominal P = 0.79) did not differ. CONCLUSIONS: Through 3 years, no between-group differences were observed in walking capacity and health-related quality of life or clinical safety outcomes between SCB angioplasty and the PCB strategy. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was higher with SCB angioplasty, with treatment effect that varied over time. Given the exploratory, nonmultiplicity-adjusted 3-year analysis, the cdTLR difference requires confirmation.
